challenges.finding: Contact follow-up: 16,205/19,853 seen (81.6%) among five reporting provinces, excluding Ituri, below 95%. Of 249 validated suspects, 142 were investigated, 111 transferred and 107 remained uninvestigated. Ituri and Nord-Ubangi alert data are ND.

PoE/PoC: two validated Biakato May suspects could not be transferred for lack of ambulance (0/2). Avakubi and Butuhe remained closed. Ituri reported 4,028 screening refusals; Tshopo and Sud-Kivu reporting completeness was 56%.

PCI/EDS: Haut-Uele reported from 4/7 zones, with missing kits and supervisors not activated in four zones. Bas-Uele reported 16/20 priority facilities without triage, 17/20 without water, and 130/632 trained providers. Visited Sud-Ubangi facilities lacked trained personnel and PCI/WASH inputs.

Care: the national isolation tile is blank. Provincial observations are separate: Ituri 409 patients/40.3% occupancy; Nord-Kivu 497/87.8%; Haut-Uele 38/21.2%; Bas-Uele 38 in isolation. Printed stocks and flows conflict; no national sum or bed denominator is inferred.

Vaccination: Ituri continued clinical trials and TUMAINI engagement. Bas-Uele reported 1,735/13,202 vaccinated (13.1%), with cold-chain startup and field-payment gaps; Bili reported 0/1,067 coverage. No established BDBV vaccine effectiveness is asserted.
Continuity: Tshopo, Bas-Uele and Sud-Ubangi submitted no pillar data. Kyaghala and Katwa corrective plans remained unfinished; free-care subsidies were insufficient in the most affected zones.

CREC: Haut-Uele resolved 5/5 feedback items within 48 hours and temporarily suspended Bolebole transit activities after a death-related incident. Bas-Uele reported and resolved three community alerts; Sud-Ubangi reported seven living alerts.

SMSPS: Ituri supported 36/44 confirmed cases under the pillar scope and covered 15/28 zones. Haut-Uele reported six new confirmed and 11 under follow-up in its pillar population; Boma Mangbetu data did not arrive. Bas-Uele support was delayed for lack of a psychologist. These are not additions to headline incidence.

Logistics and security: Buta CTE construction continued; Bas-Uele lacked diesel and office equipment. Sampling supplies were delivered in Haut-Uele and Bolebole equipment was being packed. Attacks and threats prevented Bafwasende reporting; a symptomatic contact resisted transfer. No identifying patient details are redistributed.

PSEA: 2,381 people sensitised and 59 providers briefed; cumulative 74,091 sensitised and 6,549 signatures. Only 56/151 zones were active and 2/16 partners reported, with persistent mechanism-awareness and language gaps.

priorities.recommendation: Strengthen early detection, contact follow-up, EDS and response-team security. Recommendations do not establish completed actions.
